changes_made.explanation: This paper is primarily about architectural floor plan generation (image generation), not natural language generation. While it uses text as input conditions and has text descriptions, the main outputs are floor plan images, not generated text. Therefore, it does not address NLG tasks.
All metrics are correctly extracted and properly normalized. FID, SSIM, PSNR are standard image metrics, and ARS (Architectural Reasonableness Scores) is their proposed metric.
FloorPlan-MPS is not an LLM but a specialized scoring model trained on architectural evaluations. The paper does not use LLMs as judges to evaluate generated outputs.

guideline: Functionality, scored from 1 to 10, requires annotators to assess the rationality of the functional layout, including whether the number of rooms meets requirements, whether room usage distribution is reasonable, and whether the relationships between functional areas are scientifically arranged to meet daily or commercial needs

Flow design, also scored from 1 to 10, involves reviewing the quality of flow design. Annotators focus on whether pedestrian flow is efficient, unnecessary crossings or congestions are minimized, and privacy and convenience are considered
The overall score, ranging from 1 to 10, combines the functionality and flow design scores with the annotators' subjective preferences

changes_made.explanation: Normalized criteria to consistent terminology: 'flow design' instead of 'flow', and 'overall' instead of 'overall score'. Removed duplicates and kept the main three evaluation dimensions.

overall_notes: This paper is primarily about architectural floor plan image generation, not natural language generation. While it uses NLP-inspired methods (autoregressive models, RLHF) and has text components, the main outputs are images, not generated text. The evaluation focuses on architectural quality of floor plans rather than linguistic quality of generated text.
